questions.question: A word is represented by only one set of numbers as given in any one of the alternatives. The sets of number given in the alternatives are represented by two classes of alphabets as shown in the given two matrices. The columns and rows of **Matrix-I** are numbered from 0 to 4 and that of **Matrix-II** are numbered from 5 to 9. A letter from these matrices can be represented first by its row and next by its column, for example, **‘P’** can be represented by 22, 75 etc., and **‘L’** can be represented by 20, 78, etc. Similarly, you have to identify the set for the word **“WATCH”**. **MATRIX – I** **MATRIX – II** 0 1 2 3 4
questions.solution:
The given options can be represented as,

1) 34, 00, 96, 40, 65 → WATFH

2) 02, 01, 79, 68, 10 → WNTCH

3) 02, 58, 79, 44, 65 → WATCH

4) 43, 33, 77, 03, 66 → WABCB

Thus the correct set is “02, 58, 79, 44, 65”.

questions.question:
By interchanging which two signs the equation will be correct?

58 ÷ 2 × 29 + 6 = 10
questions.solution:
After interchanging × and ÷ the equation becomes,

58 × 2 ÷ 29 + 6

⇒ 4 + 6 = 10

Thus interchanging × and ÷ the given equation becomes correct.

questions.question: If 6 $ 4 @ 6 = 18 and 7 $ 6 @ 7 = 35, then9 $ 3 @ 9 = ?
questions.solution:
Here $ means × and @ means –,

So the given expression becomes,

6 $ 4 @ 6 → 6 × 4 – 6 = 18

7 $ 6 @ 7 → 7 × 6 – 7 = 35

Similarly,

9 $ 3 @ 9 → 9 × 3 – 9 = 18

Hence the answer is 18.

questions.question:
In the following question, select the missing number from the given series.

5, 6, 10, 19, 35, ?
questions.solution:
The logic here is as follows,

5 + 1² = 6

6 + 2² = 10

10 + 3² = 19

19 + 4² = 35

Similarly,

35 + 5² = 60.

Thus next number in series is 60.

questions.question: In the following question, select the odd number pair from the given alternatives.
questions.solution:
Here the logic is as follows,

13 – 169 → 169 can be divided by 13

15 – 225 → 225 can be divided by 15

16 – 256 → 256 can be divided by 16

17 – 279 → 279 cannot be divided by 17

Thus the pair 17 – 279 is the odd pair.

questions.question:
**Direction: **In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts, read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All pens are pencils.

II. No pen is paper.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some pencils are paper.

II. Some pencils are not paper.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as follows,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/72db9f12600e497701d212901aa8badbe0f9ee260819563e548e732b2f8230e2.png] 

Conclusion:

I. Some pencils are paper → It’s possible but not definite, hence false.

II. Some pencils are not paper → Some pencils which are pen cannot be papers, hence true.

Hence only conclusion II follows.

questions.question: In a certain code language, "AIR" is written as "31" and "FOR" is written as "42". How is "WET" written in that code language?
questions.solution:
If we consider place value of alphabets,

A + I + R = 1 + 9 + 18 = 28, 28 + 3 = 31

F + O + R = 6 + 15 + 18 = 39, 39 + 3 = 42

Similarly,

W + E + T = 23 + 5 + 20 = 48, 48 + 3 = 51

Thus WET is coded as 51.
